title: Infrastructure
description: Where the application runs. Targets map to infra/vercel and infra/vm.

target.description: Which lane owns this app, and therefore WHICH ONE of the `vercel` / `vm` objects may be present. factory.py validate refuses a target=vm app that carries a `vercel` object and a target=vercel app that carries a `vm` object: .claude/scripts/lanes.py takes vercel.production_url as the URL it grades, so a vm app — which this factory never deploys — with a vercel.production_url would have a stranger's server graded as this app (mold_v1-053). The schema cannot express this conditional (the validator is a subset of JSON Schema with no if/then), so the rule lives in validate and is stated here.

health.description: The deploy's own verdict on the three health endpoints the Makefile checks (workflow /api/health, api /eve/v1/health, web /api/ops/health), written by provision.py --deploy and carried across a re-intake by intake.py; never by hand. Each value is the HTTP status the endpoint answered as a string ("200"), or "no answer". A code is not proof of isolation: the RLS verdict is read from the body and lands in datastores.postgres.rls_verified.running_app, never here.

vercel.description: Only what provision.py and intake.py write, and nothing else (additionalProperties is false, like `vm`): every key here is either read as THIS app's URL by lanes.py / the lanes' target-up gates (production_url, workflow_url, api_url) or consumed by provision.py (team, project, functions, custom_domain, crons, health). An open object let a misspelt or stranger's key validate silently (mold_v1-057); a new key must be added here WITH a description, not by reopening the object. A target=vm app must not carry this object at all — validate refuses it, see `target`.

vm.description: Only what the lane provisions, and nothing else (additionalProperties is false): the vm lane never starts a web process (infra/vm/README.md; provision.py VM_NO_PROCESS), so a URL under ANY key here would name a server this factory did not deploy. production_url was removed and is also refused by name in factory.py validate (mold_v1-053); an open object let any other spelling validate silently, so the object is now closed. A target=vercel app must not carry this object at all — validate refuses it, see `target`.

account_ref.description: Name of the secret holding the account id, never the value

secrets.description: Names of env vars the deployment must carry (values live in the target platform, never here)

secrets_user.description: Only the user can supply these (external credentials)

runtime_env.description: Non-secret env values derived from application.json; written by provision.py, never edited by hand

neon_resource.description: Vercel Marketplace Neon resource backing this app; adopted (free, unattached) or created

local_pg.description: self_hosted only: the app's own Postgres cluster on a private docker network, never a host port

deployed_at.description: The INSTANT the build now serving traffic was deployed, as an RFC 3339 date-time WITH offset — what provision.py's NOW yields: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), e.g. 2026-09-09T14:03:27+00:00. Written by provision.py --deploy at the moment the deploy finishes, never by hand. This used to be a bare date, so factory.py could only order rls_verified.at against it in whole days and a redeploy hours after the measurement still read fresh; validate now compares the two instants exactly and rejects any rls_verified.at earlier than this. The pattern is enforced (format alone is documentation to this factory's validator): a bare date, a naive time without offset, or any other spelling is a schema error. To migrate an old bare date by hand, use midnight UTC of that day (YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00+00:00) and say so in `note`: it is the earliest instant the deploy could have happened, so it is the honest conversion, but it also means a proof measured later that same day cannot be told apart from one taken before the deploy — the next --deploy writes the exact instant and ends that ambiguity.

configured_at.description: When the surface configuration was last applied to the running app. Same spelling as deployed_at (written from the same NOW): an RFC 3339 date-time WITH offset; the pattern is enforced, so a bare date or an offset-less time is a schema error (mold_v1-053).

google.description: The Google Cloud project this app's 'Continue with Google' client lives in, recorded by --set-secret GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID from the id itself (its numeric prefix is the project number). Per app: two apps may use two projects. Identifiers only, never secrets.

agent_cli.description: The application's OWN published variant of the mold's agent CLI (brand, baked-in address, its pack's agent-kit skills, its data-room description). Built from build/<app_id>/ by the mold's scripts/build-agent-cli.mjs and published by .claude/scripts/agent_cli.py. Public packages carry no credentials and no operator material.

token_ref.description: NAME of the npm publish token in the VM environment (never the value)

origin.description: the address baked into the published version; a different production_url means a new version is due

handoff_url.description: The application's published handoff page (an Artifact built by mint.py <app_id> handoff). A later session republishes to THIS url rather than creating a second page.
